summary: Hillsborough lookout in Orange County: an 80-foot state tower erected in 1947; a 2018 surplus notice asked for its removal, and trail guides say the summit tower is fenced off.

facts.status_note: Trail guides describe it as fenced off and closed; a 2018 state surplus notice asked for its removal, and whether it was removed is not confirmed.
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

access.note: Summit tower fenced off and closed to the public; the summit itself is reached on foot.

visit.trail_note: Take Virginia Cates Road to the official parking area for Occoneechee Mountain State Natural Area, then a short trek up the Summit Trail.

events.note: 80-foot tower erected by the State Forest Service; date credited to the state's 12th biennial report (1948)
State surplus auction opened on March 22, 2018; the tower stood on leased land and the landowner asked for its removal

corrections.why: The lookout-history entry is headed HILLSBOROUGH and the town is spelled Hillsborough; the state index uses the shorter form. Human review needed, since the index name may be deliberate.

notes_for_editor: The 1947 build, the 80-foot height and the 2018 surplus note all come from one page on a hobbyist site (Forest Lookouts), which quotes state biennial reports and a state surplus listing; I could not open the surplus listing itself. Linking the Hillsborough entry to the Occoneechee Mountain summit tower is an inference from two trail guides, which give no builder or date; the guides' publication dates were not checked. Two web searches did not find the outcome of the 2018 auction, so removal is unconfirmed; status is 'standing' only because the guides describe the tower as present. A Mike Legeros photo album lists a 2018-11-12 drone photo of a Hillsborough fire tower, but its page gave no readable text. No photos added.
